fix: Store the listeners as a shared slice, notification_listeners: RefCell<Rc<[(u64, ScrollNotificationListener)]>> in controller.rs, rebuilt only on add_notification_listener and on ScrollNotificationSubscription::drop (both rare). dispatch then does: let listeners = Rc::clone(&self.state.borrow().notification_listeners.borrow()); for (_, listener) in listeners.iter() { if listener(notification) { break; } }. The snapshot semantics stay the same (listeners added or dropped during dispatch do not change the current pass), but each scroll event no longer allocates a Vec and clones every Rc.

Let the caller own the buffer: pub fn offsets_for_range_into(&self, range: std::ops::Range<usize>, out: &mut Vec<f32>) { out.clear(); out.reserve(range.len() + 1); self.state.borrow().offsets_for_range(range, out); }. Change the private MeasuredExtentState::offsets_for_range to take out: &mut Vec<f32> and push (before + sum).min(f64::from(f32::MAX)) as f32 directly, and the lookup push likewise. This removes the second Vec<f32> built by .into_iter().map().collect() (f64 to f32 cannot reuse the allocation) and lets viewport layout reuse one scratch buffer per frame. Note this is a public signature change (migration: pass &mut scratch Vec instead of taking the returned Vec); values are unchanged.
Delete the line `let _ = metrics.clone();`. It is a dead Rc clone (the clone is dropped immediately and does nothing). Keep the `let metrics = Rc::new(...)` line.

Both remove and move_item flatten every row into a new Vec<Option<f32>> (one allocation of 8 bytes per row in the whole list), copy each chunk again with to_vec(), then rebuild all trees, for a change touching one or two rows. Splice only the affected chunks (as insert already does with values.splice) and rebuild the touched chunk plus the Fenwick trees, or at least move the owned flattened Vec into the chunks with split_off/drain instead of values.to_vec(). Factor the duplicated flatten-and-rechunk tail of remove and move_item into one private helper while doing so. Measure with a reorder of a 1M-row list before and after.

Avoid the temporary Vec: push the values into the tree first, then run the Fenwick build as a second in-place pass: let mut tree = Self(values.into_iter().collect::<Vec<f64>>()); for cursor in 1..=tree.0.len() { let parent = cursor + cursor.isolate_lowest_one(); if parent <= tree.0.len() { tree.0[parent - 1] += tree.0[cursor - 1]; } }. This keeps one allocation per rebuild_trees call instead of two (rebuild_trees runs on every insert, remove and move).

Use Cell::update in place of the get/set pair, here and in the other counters (lines 389-391, 406-408, 421-423, 549-551, 363-365): self.metrics.enumeration_chunks.update(|count| count + 1); Cell::update is stable on the current MSRV, and the repeated get-then-set pattern appears about ten times in the file. Alternatively add a private fn bump(cell: &Cell<u64>) helper.
Replace the three lines with: let count = self.len(); (self.len() takes the shared borrow itself and releases it, so the manual borrow and drop are not needed).

Replace the (axis: Axis, reverse: bool) pair with a single incular_config::AxisDirection parameter, which already encodes both axis and reverse (Up, Down, Left, Right): pub fn try_set_metrics_context(&self, axis_direction: incular_config::AxisDirection) -> Result<(), MetricWriteError>, then derive (axis, reverse) from it in the body. This removes the call-site ambiguity of try_set_metrics_context(Axis::Vertical, true). Public API change; migrate by passing the matching AxisDirection.
